transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-12-20
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz, Alex Chen, Samira Khan, Tom Wallace (Veridian)

Summary:
Quick onboarding kickoff to align on goals, network/security requirements, pilot scope (Dedicated trial + API), success metrics (latency/cost targets), and next steps for documentation + benchmark window.

Topics:
- High-level onboarding plan and milestones
- Environment and networking (VPC peering, egress, routes)
- Security/compliance items (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot scope: Dedicated trial for 2 weeks, target workload and datasets
- Benchmarks and telemetry: latency SLOs, cost targets, token accounting

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jared with Redwood, AE on the account, and with me are Priya, our solutions engineer, and Lena who will run onboarding. How's everyone doing at Veridian?
[00:12] Marta: Hi Jared, thanks. Marta here. All good. Excited to get started. We have been talking to Alex and Samira about the SSO and security stuff.
[00:20] Tom: Hey all, Tom from Product. We'll be driving the feature integration. Quick note: our timeline is end of Q1 for initial launch.
[00:30] Jared: Great. Goal for today is to align on milestones and actions. Priya, do you want to run through the onboarding plan?
[00:36] Priya: Yeah sure. We typically do a three-phase plan: onboarding prep (networking, credentials, access), pilot (Dedicated trial + benchmarks), then rollout with canary. For Veridian we've scoped a two-week Dedicated trial where we'll provision a reserved pool to mirror your production-ish traffic and run the benchmark harness. We'll also run a short hosted API test for early integration.
[01:05] Alex: Quick question — when you say Dedicated, is that Redwood Dedicated or the private on-prem option? We need to understand egress and whether we have to host anything ourselves.
[01:15] Priya: Good question. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model hosted by Redwood but isolated for your org. It sits in our cloud but you can request VPC peering or private network connectivity depending on region. The private / on-prem package is a separate engagement; for pilot we recommend Dedicated to keep setup lighter.
[01:33] Samira: From security we need to confirm data residency, encryption, KMS integration, and whether audit logs are exportable to our SIEM. Also SOC 2 artifacts — we need to review them.
[01:46] Lena: We'll send our SOC 2 report and security pack in the follow-up. Priya can walk through the audit log export options.
[01:53] Priya: Yep. For audit logs we can stream to your cloud account or provide S3/log forwarder. KMS is supported — we have integrations with common KMS providers, and HSM via enterprise channel. There might be some details to finalize for key rotation.
[02:10] Marta: Good — also curious about token-level billing and how to estimate cost during the pilot. We want to make sure we don't get surprised.
[02:19] Jared: We'll share a cost model template. For Dedicated the pricing is primarily the reserved capacity + token usage adjustments. Priya will run some calculations based on your expected QPS and sequence lengths.
[02:31] Tom: On success criteria: we want median latency < 250ms for chit-chat flows and 500ms for longer sequences, and cost per 1k tokens under our target — I'll share exact numbers after.
[02:42] Priya: That sounds reasonable; we'll build the benchmark profile to match. For latency we can tune batching and kv cache warmup. Note that quantization profiles may change quality slightly; we'll include evals to measure regressions.
[03:00] Alex: Network detail question: does VPC peering require static IP ranges? We're on GCP and have constrained egress.
[03:08] Priya: We can handle both peering and private-service-connect style. For GCP peering we'll need the CIDR ranges; if egress is locked down we can do an IP allowlist for our egress nodes or set up a proxy.
[03:22] Samira: Also need to confirm retention: do you retain customer prompts/inputs and for how long? We need assurances for PHI handling — though for now pilot data will be deidentified.
[03:32] Jared: By default we retain minimal logs for debugging for a short window; for enterprise we have options to disable retention or route logs to your storage. We'll put that in the security pack.
[03:41] Marta: Good. Let's talk about roles and SSO — we need RBAC so only product folks can call models and engineers can access infra consoles.
[03:50] Lena: We support SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. We'll include a mapping example in the docs.
[03:58] Tom: For integration, we plan to use your REST API first, then roll in SDKs. Any limitations on streaming or tool-calling?
[04:07] Priya: Streaming is supported; we also have function/tool-calling primitives. Some older model variants may not support streaming but the ones in our catalog do. We'll note which variants are recommended for low-latency streaming.
[04:22] Marta: On the dataset for the benchmark, we'll provide a representative sample of 50k tokens across 200 sessions. Is that enough?
[04:31] Priya: That should be fine for the initial pass. For throughput we'll need a synthetic load generator to simulate concurrent sessions — we can provide the harness.
[04:40] Alex: Good. For the Dedicated trial, will you provision GPUs in our region? Latency is sensitive to region.
[04:47] Priya: Yes, we'll attempt to provision in the same cloud region. If capacity is limited we may provision in a nearby region and route via low-latency paths; we'll document the region and expected impact.
[04:59] Samira: About compliance — if we need SOC 2 plus HIPAA, is that supported or would that require a private deployment?
[05:07] Jared: We can support HIPAA-level controls with the right contract and configurations (BAA), typically with Dedicated or Private depending on data residency and control plane requirements. We'll coordinate legal.
[05:20] Tom: Who will be the day-to-day contacts?
[05:23] Lena: I'll be the CSM lead for onboarding and coordination. Priya will own technical setup and benchmarks; Jared will be exec sponsor/owner.
[05:30] Marta: Great. Quick callouts — we have a tight window between holidays and want to start the trial first week of January. Can we get actions done before then?
[05:40] Jared: We'll try. Action items and owners we'll capture now.
[05:46] Priya: For the benchmark, I'll need the dataset and a brief on typical sequence lengths and peak QPS. I'll also ask for a couple of example prompts.
[05:55] Alex: I'll share the network diagram after this meeting.
[06:00] Samira: I'll start filling the security questionnaire. Expect to have first pass in a few days.
[06:05] Jared: Perfect. Any blockers or concerns?
[06:09] Marta: Only the usual — need clarity on cost and SOC 2 artifacts.
[06:13] Priya: We'll attach the SOC 2 pack and cost model. On tooling, we'll share the benchmark harness repo link in the follow-up.
[06:21] Tom: For rollout strategy we prefer gradual canary and feature flags to monitor regressions. Does Redwood support A/B rollouts per route?
[06:29] Priya: Yes, the Console supports route-level rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted variants. We can set canary percentages and define rollback policies.
[06:40] Marta: Any limitations around model version pinning during rollout? We need to ensure reproducibility.
[06:46] Priya: You can pin model versions and we've got a model catalog. One caveat: if you pin to an open model variant and there's a hardware-specific kernel change, performance might differ slightly across instances — we'll flag that.
[06:58] Alex: Are there recommended quantization profiles for cost savings?
[07:03] Priya: Yes, we'll recommend quantization profiles by workload; some profiles save a lot in tokens throughput but may slightly impact quality. We'll include recommended defaults for chat vs. embeddings.
[07:16] Samira: On logs export to our SIEM — is there PII redaction built-in?
[07:21] Priya: We have configurable scrubbing and redaction rules; we can also route raw logs to your storage where you control scrubbing.
[07:30] Jared: Ok, we're at the 45 minute mark; let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:36] Lena: Recap: Redwood to share onboarding plan + SOC 2 pack + cost model + benchmark harness link. Veridian to send network diagram + security questionnaire answers + sample dataset. Priya to provision Dedicated trial and run perf tests once we have network access. Schedule: aim to start trial first week of January and a 1-week follow-up after pilot kick-off.
[07:56] Tom: Sounds good. Can we get a calendar invite for the benchmark window?
[08:00] Jared: I'll send invites after we align dates — probably Jan 4–18 as tentative.
[08:05] Marta: Thanks — appreciate the clarity.
[08:08] Priya: One more technical note — for throughput testing we'll enable continuous batching and KV cache warm-up; if you have long-running sessions, we recommend a warm-up period. Also we'll instrument latency percentiles at token-level.
[08:25] Alex: Great. For the Dedicated metrics, what level of telemetry do you expose? We need per-route token counts.
[08:33] Priya: We expose token-level cost breakdowns by API key/route/model in the Console and via metrics API; you can also export to Prometheus.
[08:45] Samira: For the security artifact ask — will you need people-from Veridian to sign an NDA or is everything covered by the SOW?
[08:52] Jared: We'll handle that in legal; usually SOW and mutual NDA cover artifact exchange, but we'll confirm with Legal and include in the follow-up.
[08:59] Marta: Any known blockers for the Jan timeline?
[09:02] Priya: The only potential blocker is region capacity for Dedicated in your preferred zone; we'll surface if there's a delay. We recommend flexible window and an alternate region as fallback.
[09:15] Tom: OK. Last question — can Redwood run a short POC for private deployments if we find Dedicated doesn't meet residency?
[09:24] Jared: Yes, private deployment is possible but requires a longer lead time and a separate contract. For now pilot with Dedicated and we'll scope Private if needed.
[09:33] Marta: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Jared: We'll capture action items — Lena will follow up with the onboarding doc and links, Priya will start the trial setup, Alex and Samira will send docs from the Veridian side. Expect the follow-up with attachments within 48 hours.
[09:52] Tom: Thanks all.
[09:54] Meeting ends
